properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (measured on main): following the argument skill (a chosen principle goes in each step's `assumed`) raises reasoning_not_as_stated "assumed and never discharged" (0.5) on correct work, because the 10-17 detector reads every undischarged assumption as a proof's supposition and the 10-20 decision gave `assumed` a second meaning it never learned
properties.source: Public legal-case trial friction file F5 (flo2 design dbf39096640c196e); reflow2 main 0c567349c detect.rs, inference.rs, design-an-argument SKILL.md; git log -S
properties.statement:
OBSERVED (public legal-case trial, F5): the governing legal standards were recorded as the skill says, in each applying step's `assumed`. detect_gaps then raised reasoning_not_as_stated, "'<id>' is assumed and never discharged" (severity 0.5), twice. Nothing discharges a governing law.

MEASURED at main 0c567349c:
- getting-started/skills/design-an-argument/SKILL.md lines 31-36, 65 and 196 say a chosen principle goes in `assumed`, so positions read conditional. That is the intended result.
- detect.rs `detect_reasoning_not_as_stated` (about line 4677) pushes a gap for every assumption in inference.rs `assumptions()` (line 4303) whose discharged_by is empty. assumptions() reads only the premise link's `assumed` flag and the discharging steps. It never reads what the assumed node IS: a principle (Constraint, statement_kind proposition) or a supposition (statement_kind hypothesis).
- The detector text came in 4879171c5 on 2026-10-17 (primes-trial phase 2, proofs). The skill's use of `assumed` was settled on 2026-10-20 (this decision, option a). Nothing changed the detector after that.

CANDIDATES:
(1) The detector does not tell a chosen principle from a supposition. Confirmed: no kind is read.
(2) The trial misapplied the skill, since a legal standard is not a "principle". Partly true, because the skill has no row for law. It does not separate the two, though: a trolley-style principle in `assumed` takes the same path through the same code.
(3) The gap is right, and a principle should be discharged. Refuted by the accepted decision: conditional on a chosen principle is what an argument for and against says.

CLASS: one property carries two meanings, settled three days apart, and only one reader was written. Fix options for the owner: the detector skips assumed nodes that are not `hypothesis` (or that carry a `chosen` mark), and the skill gives a governing rule of law its own row. Not built.
